paragraphs: R’ Yishmael ben Elazar. (A Tanna of a baraita).

Hyman records his saying in Shabbat 32a: Our Rabbis taught: R’ Yishmael ben Elazar says: “For two sins, the ignorant die: calling the Holy Ark arna and calling the synagogue beit am.” (Hyman reports that Dikdukei Soferim, supplied as דק״ם, reads R’ Shimon ben Elazar.) At the end of Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:2, R’ Yishmael ben Elazar says: “The earth drinks only according to its chisum” [חיסומו, whose sense remains uncertain here].

notes.text: Hyman reports Shimon ben Elazar as a variant for Yishmael ben Elazar. The exact sense of chisum in the rain statement remains open; “muzzling” in the earlier draft did not establish it.

No new primary scalar was returned. The local heading supports Yishmael ben Elazar for רי״בא and ב״א without a new identity merge. Hyman reports the Shimon ben Elazar variant in the source supplied as דק״ם; Dikdukei Soferim is a contextual expansion, not verified letter history or a newly inspected manuscript. חיסומו remains explicit and lexically unresolved: a tool-edge sense in a different Kelim context does not establish this rain saying. End of halakhah 2 is retained, and uninspected abbreviated personal titles remain R’.

The printed Dikdukei Soferim Shabbat p. 64 aligns the printed (Yishmael) ben Elazar with “[Shimon] ben, etc.” in the manuscript column. Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:2:24 gives Yishmael, and the parallel at Avodah Zarah 3:5:6 gives Shimon. The Taanit 1:3 witness gives Shimon in a bracketed addition. The consulted Bereshit Rabbah 13:17 gives Elazar son of Shimon. These passages discuss how the soil takes up water and how tree roots are watered. Guggenheimer renders the feminine חיסומה in its setting as “hardness.” The supplied notice gives חיסומו.
